races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden

runners_data.name: Brigerbad
runners_data.note: Ran once, finished last over 6f on good, and is a true hold-up type that the map has shifted into midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; Ross O'Sullivan returns it after 32 days but the form is bare and the step to a mile is unproven.

runners_data.name: Camino Lad
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for the powerful G M Lyons yard, and three runs at a mile-plus on good ground show consistent placed efforts — the form stacks up better than most here and he is the natural second string to the stable alongside Willofthepeople.

runners_data.name: Caption This
runners_data.note: Debut runner for J A Nash with no going profile to assess; Robbie Colgan is a capable booking and Nash's first-timers deserve respect, but the lightly-raced flag and unknown ground preference add genuine uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Karrygrant
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount is the lone confirmed front-runner and will get a clean lead; six career runs show consistent placing but no wins, and the uncontested lead on a flat mile with yielding ground gives him his best chance yet of lasting home.

runners_data.name: Willofthepeople
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse returning after a lengthy 319-day absence for G M Lyons, now fitted with a tongue-tie; the lengthy layoff and previous form limited to sprint distances make this a big ask, with the midfield map slot also out of its preferred style.

runners_data.name: Misneach Sile
runners_data.note: John McConnell's runner was well beaten on its only start over a mile on good ground, and despite being a genuine hold-up type, finds itself mapped to midfield where it is unlikely to race naturally; the 5lb claimer Jack Cleary partners it.

runners_data.name: Mosel
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's colt was beaten over nine furlongs on good ground on debut and carries the DBM booking — the trainer's 15/82 14-day strike rate is strong, and this is a horse that may improve sharply for the step up to a flat mile, though it is a true hold-up type operating from a compressed midfield position.

runners_data.name: Orphanina
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly who finished tenth on her only start over eight furlongs on good ground; the lightly-raced caveat applies and she carries a "fades in finish" warning, making a forward result hard to envisage from a cold reading.

runners_data.name: Peshwari Nan
runners_data.note: 179 days off the track for McConnell is a significant concern, and two previous runs on standard ground saw her finish eighth and twelfth; a genuine hold-up runner placed into the midfield map due to overcrowding, facing a significant fitness question on return.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Three runs for Joseph O'Brien all ended in double-figure finishes over longer trips, and the "fades in finish" tag combined with the 7-day turnaround suggest connections are finding her feet rather than targeting a win here.

runners_data.name: Star Of Beauty
runners_data.note: K J Condon's filly has placed four times from six runs, all at eight furlongs on good ground, and W J Lee is a strong jockey booking; she is a natural prominent type who should track Karrygrant closely and represents the most straightforward profile for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Sweetie Too
runners_data.note: Two poor efforts on good ground at eight furlongs for Brendan Duke, and the "fades in finish" warning is borne out by the form string; 22 days between runs is fine but the ability level appears modest.

runners_data.name: Tax Me Later
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Daniel McLoughlin, partnered by Nathan Crosse; the going profile and style are entirely unknown, and with a small trainer operation this is one of the least-exposed quantities in a race already full of lightly-raced types.

runners_data.name: Whatsin The Stars
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's filly has finished 15th and 11th on her two starts at eight furlongs on good ground, fitted with a hood; two consecutive poor efforts and a "fades in finish" flag make a big improvement hard to justify.

runners_data.name: Wooloongabba
runners_data.note: McConnell's third runner in this race, finished 11th and 13th on sprint trips on good ground, and like stablemates Peshwari Nan and Misneach Sile is a genuine hold-up type shifted into midfield on the map; the shortest trips in its history make the mile step speculative.

races.paceDynamic: Karrygrant is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner maiden and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on yielding ground at Bellewstown. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a lone leader over a flat mile in these conditions typically sets an honest but unspectacular tempo, with the race likely to compress through the middle stages before quickening from the two-furlong pole. Star Of Beauty and Camino Lad are the most credible prominent types capable of tracking Karrygrant, putting them in an enviable position to pounce if the pace does not fully test stamina. This shape — a single, uncontested leader setting a moderate-to-fair tempo — most strongly favours horses that can race prominently or just off the pace, converting a tactical advantage into a late burst rather than demanding a relentless staying test. This field contains more hold-up and midfield types than the map can genuinely accommodate: Peshwari Nan, Mosel, Misneach Sile, Brigerbad, and others are natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield slots on the map, but Star Of Beauty and Camino Lad are the runners most likely to actually secure prominent tracking positions in real running.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Karrygrant Controls; Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Karrygrant bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but measured pace, allowing the closest trackers to sit within two lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: Karrygrant dictates the fractions unchallenged and the tempo is moderate enough to keep the field compact; horses who tracked closely into the straight arrive with energy in reserve and quicken past a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Prominent Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Karrygrant sets a dawdling gallop that produces a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow pace compresses the field entirely, nullifying any hold-up advantage and turning the race into a sharp dash for home; horses with a forward position and tactical speed thrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Karrygrant, pressured unexpectedly or simply going faster than anticipated on yielding ground, sets a genuinely searching pace.
scenarios.body: A true end-to-end test over a mile on soft-ish turf stretches the field and saps the leaders, giving any genuinely forward-travelling hold-up type a rare chance to emerge late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 15 causes interference and positional scrambling in the early stages, disrupting the pace shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With so many horses shuffled out of their natural positions into a congested midfield, erratic early running could produce an atypical winner who weaves through traffic late.

watchPoints.text: Star Of Beauty's ability to secure the prominent tracking position directly behind Karrygrant is the key positioning battle — if she gets there uncontested, she becomes the most dangerous runner in the race.

Karrygrant's solo lead could turn dangerously slow if Ben Coen opts to conserve the horse; watch the early splits, as a truly dawdling gallop would undermine any hold-up runner's chance entirely and hand prominence a near-certain advantage.

With 15 runners and a large cluster of midfield horses unable to get their natural positions, early crowding on the inside rail at Bellewstown could cause interference — horses drawn wide may be forced to race wide throughout, costing valuable ground on the tight circuit.

Mosel (DBM) and Camino Lad (Keane) carry the two most notable jockey bookings for hold-up/midfield types — if either can improve their position rounding the home bend, they are capable of posting a late run into the placings even if the pace shape does not fully suit.

The going report confirms the ground is yielding throughout the card, not just good-to-soft as declared — this stamina test at a flat mile on genuinely soft turf will expose any runner whose form is built on faster surfaces, and Peshwari Nan and Willofthepeople (both standard-ground form) should be watched with that in mind.

races.name: Ploughman Bar & Grill Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Cian Hughes and Colin Keane, 11 days fresh; goes on good and has similar-going form of 2 wins and 5 placed from 14 runs — the horse to beat purely because it controls the pace in a field that cannot organise to pressure it early.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Sheila Lavery with a disappointing recent string of 9-7-0-0-6 and zero wins or places in soft-adjacent conditions from 12 efforts; 19 days since last run and likely to need a pace that never materialises in this shape.

runners_data.name: Wegotogether
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator returning from a lengthy 101-day break for Gavin Cromwell, who is in decent form at 7/27 over 14 days; has only run on 6 or 7 furlongs recently — the step to a mile is a slight unknown and the layoff is a meaningful flag.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: A hold-up runner who was winning on soft/standard at 7f earlier in the year but has produced two consecutive zeros and carries a finish-fade warning; the slow pace in this shape does not help a horse who needs the race to truly develop before landing a blow.

runners_data.name: Distillate
runners_data.note: 148 days off the track for Adrian McGuinness, who has been placing horses at a productive 5/25 rate over the last fortnight; this hold-up type has recent Haydock and standard-ground form at 7-8f and the extended absence is the clearest risk flag here.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's hold-up runner, who returned just 9 days ago and has been tumbling down the field in a long run of poor efforts; carries a finish-fade alert and has struggled badly over 8f on good, making this shape — slow pace, tactical race — far from ideal.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Front-running type who is prominent enough to track Launch Time if given the chance; only three runs on record, all on good at 7f and 12f, and carries the finish-fade flag — likely to grab a prominent pitch for Denise Foster's yard but may find the trip stretching stamina over a mile on a yielding surface.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by nature — E D Delany's six-year-old has finished 8-10-10-11 in recent runs and has form over longer trips; the redistribution to midfield reflects the glut of hold-up runners rather than a change of style, and the fade flag compounds a difficult outlook.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: T J O'Mara's veteran has a win on soft and placed efforts at this trip; the horse is a true hold-up type whose map position in midfield is a consequence of the overcrowded rear, not a reflection of how it will race — the soft-ground winning form is the single angle worth noting.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's four-year-old has placed form at 8f on good going and shaped with promise; genuinely settles and waits, so the fact it appears in midfield on the map is a mapping artefact — it will race deeper than shown and needs a stronger gallop than Launch Time is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Prominent type for a moderate yard and a 7lb claimer; has a string of seventh and eighth finishes at this trip on good and standard going, and the pace map is the one shape that suits — tracking Launch Time from a prominent pitch gives it more chance than its OR of 43 implies.

runners_data.name: Tullyesker
runners_data.note: Donal Kinsella's hold-up four-year-old, last seen 55 days ago, has finished 8-8-12-17 in recent starts and carries a finish-fade flag; the horse's true place is further back than the map shows — it needs a strong gallop it is unlikely to get, and the layoff adds risk.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: A hold-up type whose entire recent career has been over 13-14 furlongs; the drop to a flat mile in a tactical race is a dramatic change of context for Liam McAteer's runner, and the finish-fade warning on a horse built for staying distances makes its chance very slim here.

runners_data.name: Hale Bopp
runners_data.note: P Sweeney's eight-year-old has placed at 8f on good and has the most recent form at the right trip; 75 days since last run and naturally sits in the hold-up group — the map puts it in midfield only because there is no room behind, and it will need luck in running to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount on Seamus Fahey's veteran, who has been running at 9-10f on good and soft; a hold-up operator in reality, the midfield slot on the map is borrowed space — the finish-fade flag and preference for longer trips than a flat mile are genuine concerns.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: The ten-year-old for R Donohoe has been remarkably consistent at 7-8f on good, with a pattern of 5-6-7 finishes; prominent by style, just 5 days since last run, and the tubed headgear is noted — if any of the stalkers are to capitalise on Launch Time's controlled pace, this horse's tactical profile is the most suited.

races.paceDynamic: Launch Time is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Pettus Bridge and Rampage capable of tracking up prominently, the pace is set to be modest and largely uncontested on this flat Bellewstown mile on yielding ground. A single, unhurried gallop-setter over a trip where the bend into the straight compresses the field means those on the pace will hold their energy deep into the race — a shape that historically rewards horses who can sit just off the leader and mount a sustained run rather than those who need a strongly-run race to deliver a finishing burst. The bulk of this field are genuine hold-up types but so many are clustered at the rear that the first turn will shuffle them back further than ideal, eroding their chance of ever getting competitive. Accordingly, this race shape squarely favours prominent or close-up runners who can control their own destiny behind Launch Time, rather than those dependent on a fast pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time controls throughout at a steady clip and the hold-up runners are left with too much to do in the straight.
scenarios.body: Launch Time dictates a sedate rhythm, burning minimal energy, and kicks clear turning in before the pack can organise a coherent challenge from deep; on yielding ground the leader's stamina edge compounds the advantage. Prominent types who track closely — Pettus Bridge and Rampage — are best placed to challenge, but neither has the class to overhaul a confident front-runner in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate but Brains, Rampage or Pettus Bridge track Launch Time aggressively and outstay it in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The stalkers sit within two or three lengths of the leader throughout, and the modest fractions on a stamina-testing yielding surface mean the race is decided by who has the most left inside the final 100 yards; Brains, with a strong recent record in similar conditions, profiles well for this shape. Rampage and Pettus Bridge add pressure but both carry finish-fade flags that soften their claims.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply early or scrimmaging causes the front group to burn fuel, leaving the door open for mid-pack runners to deliver a late run.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up types compressed into midfield, a chaotic first half-mile could see the gaps arrive earlier than expected, but the going is unlikely to generate a truly true-run test at this class level. Draiocht, who has winning form on soft and a history of mid-race improvement, and La Campanella, placed on good at this trip, are the most credible closers even though their mapped position overstates how far back they will actually race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Contest
scenarios.trigger: If the large, unbalanced field loses shape entirely — bunching, interference and slow early fractions creating a sprint finish that randomises the result.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners on a flat course, a falsely slow pace can compress the field to a wall at the two-furlong mark, producing a rough-and-tumble dash where clean runs are decisive and form lines count for little. Any of the prominent or midfield types finding daylight first can prevail, but the horses most exposed to traffic — the true hold-up runners shuffled to the rear — are the biggest losers in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Launch Time (Colin Keane) faces no pace pressure whatsoever — watch whether Keane elects to steal the race with a long run from the front or sits quietly; either way, any drift in the market would be significant given the horse controls the tempo entirely.

With 16 runners on a flat course, the initial positioning battle at the first turn could see the large contingent of hold-up types — Draiocht, La Campanella, Hale Bopp, Bang Po and others — shuffled even further back than expected, effectively ending their race before the straight.

Brains runs just 5 days after its last start — watch for any signs of staleness in the paddock or any market drift, as the horse's prominent style makes it the most interesting tactical rival to Launch Time but a quick turnaround at age 10 is a risk.

The going is confirmed yielding rather than the official good-to-soft — any horse whose form profile leans on faster conditions (Launch Time has 2W5P in similar going but several others have no yielding evidence) may find the surface softer than their record implies.

Distillate returns from 148 days off and Wegotogether from 101 days — watch both in the market; if either is supported despite the layoff, trainer intent is likely signalled, particularly McGuinness (5/25 at 14 days) and Cromwell (7/27), both in form yards.

races.name: Ploughman Bar & Grill Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Albion Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has posted finishes of 9-8-4-8-9 recently with zero wins or places on similar going; 60 days off and Luke McAteer takes over, but the pattern of running offers little encouragement in a competitive 15-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Givehertilxmas
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a major booking for Gerard Keane's yard which has struck at 1 from 7 runners in the last fortnight; the hood is on and she showed a placed effort at 3 last time, though her hold-up style means she needs something to go wrong up front.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's charge ran just nine days ago and comes here as a genuine hold-up horse — though there are so many rear-runners in this field that getting into his preferred deep position will be natural; two wins and six places on similar going in 15 attempts is a solid profile, and the trainer has a runner in form (1/14, T14).

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: WJ Lee takes the ride for Denis Hogan who has saddled two winners from 22 in the past fortnight; has placed form at this level and showed a second and fourth in recent starts, though he has not won in 15 attempts on good-equivalent ground.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this consistent hold-up type who has three places from nine similar-going runs; showed a second last time over 10f before reverting to a mile today, and the slight drop back in trip could sharpen his finish.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, Adam Caffrey rides for Adrian McGuinness who has won 5 of 25 in the last 14 days — a yard in cracking form; one win and three places from nine runs on good going and a STYLE_FIT flag means he is racing in his natural role but a style-fit tempers confidence slightly if the pace shapes unexpectedly.

runners_data.name: Think About It
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-class booking for a modest yard, which merits attention; at heart a hold-up horse, he has stepped up significantly in trip in recent runs (10f-14f) and dropping back to 8f on yielding ground is an unknown quantity — his style-fit discount applies because this race has too many rear-runners already.

runners_data.name: Bright Dick
runners_data.note: Returns from a mammoth 775-day absence, which is the dominant concern here; Robbie Colgan partners for Luke Comer and the horse has placed form from this distance and similar going in the past, but such a lengthy layoff makes it extremely difficult to assess his current condition.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan's booking gives this Donal Kinsella-trained four-year-old a significant jockey upgrade; has won at 8f on good going and placed on another occasion, but as a true hold-up horse in a field loaded with rear-runners, he will be competing for space at the back rather than anywhere near his optimal mid-race position.

runners_data.name: Oitentinha
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche partners for Oliver McKiernan and the horse carries a fades-in-finish flag alongside being a hold-up type repositioned to midfield on the pace map; recent form reads 9-9-9-12-8 and there is no obvious angle to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Chant d'Or
runners_data.note: Returning from 308 days off for Daniel McLoughlin, who has gone 0 from 20 in the last fortnight; a fades-in-finish flag and a limited three-run form profile showing 0-0-0 makes this one extremely difficult to recommend, with the long layoff the overriding concern.

runners_data.name: Sunday Sovereign
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for GA Kingston who carries a fades-in-finish flag and has placed three times from 13 runs on similar going without winning; prominent position is natural and she can track the pace, but the age and the late-fade tendency work against her in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Ben Coen is a strong jockey booking for Denise Foster's yard; as a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the pace map by the volume of rear-runners, she needs to be noted for a placed effort at 8f last time and a second over 10f two runs ago — the drop back to a mile and the crowded hold-up group are the limiting factors.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh is an excellent pilot and ran just 10 days ago, suggesting connections see him as fit and ready; a hold-up horse with one place in 15 runs on good going, he is another genuine rear-runner forced to compete for a deep position in this heavily back-loaded field.

runners_data.name: Monzoon
runners_data.note: Returns from 256 days off with apprentice Sadhbh Tormey taking the ride for P Sweeney who has just one runner in the last 14 days; the fades-in-finish flag and a recent record showing 0-0-0-0-0 over this distance and going make this a very difficult proposition on current evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Land Of The Giants is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner mile handicap and, with no other genuine pace-setter to press him, he is poised to control proceedings from the front at a comfortable, unhurried tempo on yielding ground at Bellewstown. Bright Dick and Sunday Sovereign are the only other horses mapped to prominent positions, meaning the head of the race will be thinly populated and Land Of The Giants can dictate exactly how fast this is run. The overwhelming majority of the field are hold-up types — Dinamine, Think About It, Micasso, Oitentinha, Chant d'Or, Duchess Anne, Master Garvey and Monzoon have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many true rear-runners for the visual to accommodate them all at the back; Land Of The Giants, Bright Dick and Sunday Sovereign are most likely to secure their natural position at the front. A single, uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable pace on yielding ground over a flat mile strongly favours a prominent or tracking profile — horses who can sit just off the pace in the first two or three positions will be best placed when the race develops in the final two furlongs, rather than those forced to close from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants bowls along unchallenged and sets a true but measured pace, with no rival willing or able to go with him.
scenarios.body: Land Of The Giants dictates every yard at a comfortable gallop and still has enough in reserve to repel challengers; the horses who track him closely — Bright Dick and Sunday Sovereign — are handed a golden rail to chase.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Bright Dick and Sunday Sovereign push up alongside Land Of The Giants early, creating a more genuine pace that burns off outsiders.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo compresses the mid-race fractions, and horses who settle just behind the lead quarter — Medieval Night and Perfect Judgement — get a pace to aim at without overextending their stamina on the yielding surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front trio tie each other up, allowing a handful of hold-up horses to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Dinamine has winning form on good ground over this trip and, if allowed to travel sweetly through the race, could produce a late burst; Micasso has also shown winning ability at this distance and going combination and could emerge as the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants is taken on hard from the outset and the field concertinas, producing a slowly-run race that turns into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A ragged, falsely-run contest compresses the field and removes pace advantages entirely, handing an edge to horses with raw ability and a sharp turn of foot; Givehertilxmas and Medieval Night, each with headgear and Colin Keane/WJ Lee in the saddle, have the class profile to exploit a muddling finish.

watchPoints.text: Land Of The Giants sets the only reliable pace in the race — watch whether Bright Dick or Sunday Sovereign immediately challenge him at the break, because if they do, the pace dynamic shifts materially and front-end stamina becomes the decisive factor.
Dinamine ran just nine days ago and Michael Mulvany's yard has a runner in T14 form — watch for market support; if he fires fresh he is the likeliest beneficiary of any mid-race collapse.

Bright Dick returns from 775 days off and any early exuberance from a freshened-up horse could disrupt the settled tempo Land Of The Giants is expected to set — monitor his behaviour in the early furlongs.

Colin Keane on Givehertilxmas and Seamie Heffernan on Micasso are two of the highest-calibre jockeys in the race; watch the market closer to post time, as both horses are difficult to assess from form alone and jockey bookings of this quality on outsiders sometimes signal stable intent.

The going report consistently reads Yielding for the 5:30 mile at Bellewstown despite the official Good to Soft designation — horses with proven form on soft or yielding ground hold a clear advantage and any runner whose form figures come exclusively on good-to-firm or faster surfaces should be treated with caution.

races.name: Gleeson's Bar, Drogheda, Home Of Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator stepping up from 7f to 8f in soft-ground form (3P from 3 runs on similar), but struggling for wins (0 from 12 career), and a large field limits the clear passage this style demands; trainer Gerard O'Leary has one winner from eight in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Adrian McGuinness who will look to make all, but has just one placing from six runs on soft-ground equivalents and has drifted back to 8f after mostly 7f runs; wears a visor, 13 days since last run, and faces a genuine battle for the lead with Elusive Path.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with a win 16 days ago at 7f on good ground, now stepping up to 8f which stretches his profile; two wins and three places in 15 starts, runs for Adrian McGuinness alongside Exquisite Acclaim, with trainer recording five winners from 25 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent 15-from-15 record on good or similar ground including three wins, and consistent placings at 8f; Andrew Slattery rides and trains, a dual role that tends to sharpen focus, and this horse is one of the few capable of genuinely tracking from second in a busy field.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up performer with six placings from 14 runs on soft-ground equivalents and zero wins, 47 days off the track; has strong placing form at 8f and 9f, but the large field and her style make a clean run difficult, and trainer Sheila Lavery has one from five in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type trained by JP Murtagh, 11-from-11 on good-ground runs in form — solid placing record but only one win; stepping from 7f to 8f for the first time in this field, Ben Coen takes the ride and the horse's tactical position will depend on how quickly the field settles.

runners_data.name: Pillar Of Hope
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose natural mode is hold-up racing but who finds himself placed in midfield on the map due to the number of closers in this field; trainer P Sweeney has zero from one in 14 days, the horse has recent form over longer trips (9f-13f) and the 8f trip here is likely short of his best.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Holds a visor and a hold-up racing profile, yet the field density means he cannot find his favoured position at the rear; four-year-old with one win from 15 runs on good ground, recent form figures of 37-077 show no momentum, and W McCreery has three wins from 19 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Elusive Path
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old front-runner for G M Lyons with a consistently placed record (3-2-3 from three runs) and all form on good or soft ground — ideally suited to this 8f trip; Colin Keane's presence is a major upgrade in craft if the pace needs managing, and 41 days off the track is the only minor question.

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who has placed three times at 8f-10f on good ground including a win, though the visor suggests he can be keen; three-year-old for John S O'Donoghue who has zero wins from three in 14 days, and the step back to 8f from recent 10f runs may be a positive if stamina had been questioned.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old trained by R P Cody with moderate recent form (including a 9th last time out on good), ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle whose class is the main asset; form at 8f on good-to-soft (3rd) is encouraging, but zero trainer wins from six in 14 days and a busy field temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Has winning and placing form at 6f-7f on good ground — a notably shorter trip than today's 8f — and is a hold-up type whose true positioning at the back of the field will be hard to achieve in this 18-runner crowd; style fit is compromised here, though recent form (1st, 2nd) is sharp if the trip is not a stretch.

runners_data.name: Goofy Gander
runners_data.note: A hold-up three-year-old returning after 76 days off, trained by Mrs John Harrington who has two wins from 32 in 14 days; wears a hood and form on soft or yielding going is limited (zero places from five runs on soft), and the layoff plus inability to settle in a favoured rear position work against him.

runners_data.name: Dream Legend
runners_data.note: Has two wins on good-to-soft ground at 8f showing that the going and trip are not concerns, but a 'fades in finish' tag is a significant flag at a mile; 54 days off the track, three-year-old for E D Delany, and while natural ability is there, the tendency to stop late plus out-of-role positioning in this field soften the outlook.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly whose best placing (3rd, 8f, good) shows she can stay and handle this ground, but she has zero wins from 14 starts and a cluttered field makes a clean late run from the rear very difficult; trainer Jack Foley has one winner from five in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran for Adrian McGuinness with form figures including wins at 8f on good ground, and visor is retained; though shown in midfield on the pace map, this horse's natural mode leans toward hold-up tactics, and at 125lbs carrying weight is a consideration in a competitive 18-runner handicap — trainer in strong form (5 from 25 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins and five places from 15 starts on good or similar ground, including a recent second at 8f; one of the few who can genuinely adopt a prominent role in this field, and the 8f trip is proven — no jockey listed is the key unknown going into final declarations.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Has winning form at 8f on good ground and a recent 2nd at 8f, suggesting form is live, but this hold-up type cannot secure the rear position she needs in an 18-runner field; Gavin Cromwell sends her out in strong trainer form (7 from 27 in 14 days), and the 119lbs weight gives a significant pull on some rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Exquisite Acclaim and Elusive Path are the two confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner field, and with Colin Keane aboard Elusive Path and Sam Coen on Exquisite Acclaim, both handlers will be looking to establish early position — a contested lead is virtually certain, setting an honest-to-strong gallop on yielding ground over a mile at Bellewstown. The pace will be genuine from the outset, meaning those who are dragged into a battle up front risk stopping, while horses able to track the action from second or third without expending needless energy are ideally placed. A large number of runners — Pillar Of Hope, Goofy Gander, Bundle Of Interest, Rappell, Goofy Gander, Dream Legend, Girl Bear, Comfort Line and Reponse Finale — are natural hold-up types who will be unable to find their preferred ground in a field this size, with Zaraahmando and Felix Somary the most credible prominent horses behind the two pace-setters who can actually secure that position. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types with proven form on soft/yielding ground who can track a genuine gallop and sustain their effort in the final two furlongs, rather than true hold-up horses who face a troubled passage in an 18-runner field running at pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Acclaim and Elusive Path fight for the front and set a genuine pace that stretches the field, leaving hold-up types with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop on yielding ground will see the pace collapse approaching the final quarter-mile, rewarding horses that have tracked efficiently from a prominent position and can sustain their effort; the mile trip on this ground will expose any horse with stamina questions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Elusive Path settles into a comfortable lead under Colin Keane and dictates a controlled, measured gallop that denies others the tempo to run them down.
scenarios.body: Elusive Path has placed in all three career starts including twice at 8f+ on good-to-soft ground, and a steadier pace from the front would play to its unbeaten-in-placing consistency; Colin Keane's tactical intelligence is a key factor if the pace dynamic becomes less frenetic than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners burn each other out at a strong pace and a wave of horses from the middle of the pack time their run to sweep through late.
scenarios.body: Goal Exceeded is proven over 8f on good ground with two wins at 7f and strong recent form, while Morehampton and Anvika both have placing form on similar going and could benefit if pace is truly extreme; however, many nominal midfield runners here are redistributed hold-up types, softening this scenario's likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly punishing and the entire field is strung out, creating a race where genuine hold-up horses can pick up late.
scenarios.body: This scenario is undermined significantly by the redistribution reality — horses like Rappell, Reponse Finale and Dream Legend are true hold-up types but will struggle for clear passage in an 18-runner field, and the yielding ground at Bellewstown historically rewards those able to be involved earlier.

watchPoints.text: Elusive Path and Exquisite Acclaim — watch which of these two front-runners goes for the early lead at the break, as the one forced to race in the second position may tire and stop, dramatically altering the pace shape in the final quarter-mile.

Zaraahmando — with 15-from-15 form on today's ground type and a genuinely prominent style that can be delivered in this field, any drift in the market or jockey change should be noted as a significant betting signal in a race where prominent spots are scarce.

Goal Exceeded — running for the same trainer as Exquisite Acclaim (Adrian McGuinness), raising the question of which horse receives stable support and whether a team-based tactical decision shapes how aggressively Exquisite Acclaim leads.

Reponse Finale — Gavin Cromwell's 7-from-27 14-day strike rate is the best in this field, and despite the redistribution challenge for hold-up horses, a lightly-weighted runner with recent winning form at this exact trip and going deserves monitoring for market moves near post time.

Dream Legend — the 'fades in finish' flag is a meaningful physical concern at a mile on yielding ground in a field of 18; watch for any positive market move, which may suggest connections have addressed the issue, but treat any short price with caution given that flag.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden

runners_data.name: Bit Of A Buzz

runners_data.name: Lion Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Kieran Cotter has struck at a modest 0/2 in the last 14 days and this runner has only one start — an 11th over 6f on good — but the confirmed lead-seeking style means a straight battle for the rail with Bit Of A Buzz is inevitable; the fade-in-finish flag is a meaningful concern when a contested pace on yielding ground is the likely outcome.|

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's runner has a patchy record (best effort a third over 5f on standard going) and is a genuine hold-up type that cannot get its natural position in this field shape; the 0.90 style-fit discount applies, and with 32 days since last run and headgear noted, its chance hinges almost entirely on the front end imploding spectacularly.|

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Eddie & Patrick Harty's runner has shown modest form (best a 4th over 5f on good) with a 7lb claimer aboard in Jessica O'Gorman, but the prominent style suits the likely race shape well — sitting just behind the contested lead duo and pressing home from two furlongs out is exactly the tactical position this scenario throws up.|

runners_data.name: Magna Fortuna
runners_data.note: Two very poor runs (13th and 11th) on good ground over middle trips signal a horse well out of its depth here; Nathan Crosse rides but the fade-in-finish flag combined with zero placed form and a 56-day absence gives little grounds for optimism regardless of the pace shape that develops.|

runners_data.name: Annie Batt
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides his own runner, who showed a placed effort (2nd over 5f on good) suggesting some ability; a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on this map because rear positions are oversubscribed, meaning it is unlikely to race in its natural role, and the style-fit discount tempers its prospects meaningfully.|

runners_data.name: Sadie Rose
runners_data.note: F G Hand's runner has finished 14th and 12th in two starts, both over 6f, and carries the fade-in-finish flag — running only two days since its last outing is an unusual pattern that warrants caution; hold-up style means it faces the same positional squeeze as the other rear-ward types in this pace-heavy field.|

runners_data.name: Tango Club
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's runner has two modest finishes (5th and 6th over 6f on good) but shows the best recent trajectory of the genuine hold-up types; 20 days since last run is routine, and while a natural closer in a race that may not set up for late runs, it remains the most plausible beneficiary if the front end does collapse in the closing stages.|

races.paceDynamic: Lion Of Fortune and Bit Of A Buzz are both confirmed front-runners and will push each other from the gates over this 5f on yielding ground at Bellewstown, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead. With two leaders fighting for supremacy, the pace is likely to be honest-to-strong for a maiden sprint on this surface, which historically drains stamina reserves and leaves exposed front-runners vulnerable in the final furlong. Annie Batt and Belle Island are natural hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because the field holds more rear-ward runners than can all settle at the back in this shape — Annie Batt, with a placed effort over 5f on good ground, is the more likely of the two to get a workable position. This contested pace shape favours horses who can sit just off the speed in a prominent or close-midfield berth and produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs rather than those who need to make up significant ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lion Of Fortune and Bit Of A Buzz burn each other off early and a prominent tracker picks up the pieces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two leaders set a searingly honest tempo on yielding ground that leaves both emptying late, handing the initiative to any horse sitting second or third at halfway; the 5f distance on this going does not forgive front-runners who race hard against each other. Best Love and Annie Batt, both capable of stalking the pace from prominent or just off positions, are best-placed to capitalise as the leaders tie up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Sustain, Front Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If one of Lion Of Fortune or Bit Of A Buzz establishes a clear advantage early and is not run into the ground by the other.
scenarios.body: Should one front-runner dominate and the other fail to press, the yielding ground actually becomes workable for the leader as the gallop settles to an honest rather than suicidal level; a front-runner with a clean break in a small field of eight can control the race entirely on this tight track. Lion Of Fortune's high OR and Bit Of A Buzz's consistent placed form make both candidates, with whichever gets the cleaner start most likely to dictate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel burns out both leaders entirely and ground-saving hold-up horses can produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Yielding ground over 5f can produce late collapses from exhausted leaders, theoretically opening the door for closers, but Annie Batt and Belle Island are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to secure their natural position in this shape, significantly reducing the scenario's probability. Tango Club, showing a slight improvement profile in its two runs, represents the closest genuine threat from the chasing pack if the front end falls apart completely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners check each other's stride rather than truly sprinting clear and the field concertinas, producing a messy, hard-to-read finish.
scenarios.body: In a small field of eight on yielding ground, if neither leader fully commits and the pace drops, the race can compress into a group finish where positional luck and a late kick from midfield types becomes decisive; Best Love or Magna Fortuna could benefit from a more moderate tempo. Magna Fortuna's poor form figures make this a low-probability route to relevance, and the scenario itself is the least likely given that both Lion Of Fortune and Bit Of A Buzz are confirmed lead-seeking types.

watchPoints.text: Lion Of Fortune and Bit Of A Buzz will fight for the front, and whichever fails to dominate the early exchange on yielding ground is immediately compromised — watch the first two furlongs to see which gives way and which commits to a lung-busting lead.|

Annie Batt and Belle Island are genuine hold-up horses that cannot reach the back of this field in practice; if either is forced to race prominently rather than in its natural position, its chance should be significantly discounted regardless of market moves.|

Sadie Rose runs just two days after its last start — monitor any market drifts as a sign the stable is not confident, and note the fade-in-finish flag makes it a poor candidate in a race where the finish is likely to be hard-fought on yielding ground.|

The entire going report for this card reads Yielding across all distances — the stated Good to Soft card going is softer than advertised, and any runner with a going concern on genuinely soft or yielding ground should be treated with extra caution, particularly front-runners who will have covered more ground at speed.|

races.name: Gibney's Of Gormanstown Handicap

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Trained by J P Murtagh and carrying 143lbs, this 3yo has strong 5f form on Good going — including a win and a second in recent starts — and a prominent style that slots perfectly into the predicted race shape; sim-going record of 12/13 with 1W 7P is compelling.

runners_data.name: Prairie Girl
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f on Standard and has shown up at 5f on Good going, and while her sim-going record on truly similar conditions is thin (0W1P from 4), her naturally prominent style and fresh legs (16 days) make her dangerous if the leaders tire as expected.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator who will look to come from the rear, but his recent form at 5f on Good shows a third as his best effort from 10 attempts on similar going; the 10-day turnaround is tight, and his 0W3P sim-going record suggests he hits the frame more than he wins.

runners_data.name: Bad Boy Rizz
runners_data.note: A genuine closer with a win at 5f on Soft and a second at 6f on Good, he is the most credible hold-up sprinter in the field if the pace truly collapses late; Shane Foley takes the ride which is a notable booking, and his trainer has been active (1 from 18 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters, ridden by 7lb claimer Sadhbh Tormey, who has shown ability to go forward but whose recent form includes several mid-field finishes over 6f-7f; dropping back to 5f is the right move, but the burden of making the running with a rival in Bye Bye Now likely increases his chance of fading.

runners_data.name: Buddy Batt
runners_data.note: Lightly used recently (58 days off), this 5yo has a win and a place at 5f on Standard going but no wins on sim-going from 7 attempts; Ronan Whelan is a positive addition to the saddle, and he would suit a scenario where the pace eases enough to allow a late-midfield run.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good here 9 days ago and has been placed at the same course and distance on multiple occasions — his 14 from 15 sim-going record with 2 wins is the standout course-and-going statistic in the race; the tight turnaround is a mild flag but his trainer has had success at the meeting.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 3yo has a win on similar going and decent placed efforts at 5f, but as a genuine hold-up type in a field loaded with pace, the race shape is likely to push him closer to midfield than he prefers; his STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 reflects this displacement.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: McCreery's 5yo has an excellent sim-going record (2W7P from 11) and genuine class at this level, but as a confirmed hold-up horse who will struggle to get his natural position in this fast-paced scenario, his effectiveness is compromised; the 9-day return is fine, and Leigh Roche is consistent, but the race shape works against him.

runners_data.name: Asdana
runners_data.note: Returning after 79 days off, this 4yo filly has a win on Soft and a placed effort at 5f on similar going, but the long absence combined with being a true hold-up type in a race where her position will be compromised — STYLE_FIT 0.93 — makes this a tougher ask than her bare form suggests; the 7lb claimer aboard adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Bye Bye Now
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner with a win at 5f on Standard, ridden by Siobhan Rutledge; his pattern of trading early fractions with another pace-setter on yielding ground makes him a likely early-race influence but a doubtful finisher, and his sim-going record of 0W1P from 2 is sparse.

races.paceDynamic: Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now are the two confirmed front-runners in an 11-runner field over 5f on yielding ground at Bellewstown, and both will attempt to lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft solo lead. The resulting pace is likely to be honest-to-strong for the conditions, which on a flat 5f course with no bends to disrupt positioning should stretch the field into a clear shape by halfway. Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, and Asdana are all genuine hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural rear position with this level of pace in front, and will be shuffled closer to midfield than ideal. This race shape — two fighting leaders burning fuel on yielding ground — strongly favours prominent racers with tactical speed who can sit just off the pace and pounce when the front two tie up inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now push hard from the start and exhaust each other on yielding ground, setting up a race for the stalkers.
scenarios.body: The two leaders trade blows through the first three furlongs and their effort becomes increasingly laboured on soft-leaning ground, leaving them vulnerable to horses travelling comfortably just behind; prominent racers with good 5f form on similar going are ideally placed to sweep past. Namiid and Prairie Girl, both proven prominent operators with solid Goodish-ground form at 5f, are perfectly profiled to benefit from this textbook pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Brave It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is less truly contested than expected and one front-runner gains a clear advantage early, allowing them to control tempo and conserve enough energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: Should Bye Bye Now or Smoke Them Out manage to clear their rival quickly off the break, they could find a rhythm on the flat Bellewstown track and convert the lead into a front-running win before the hold-up horses can close; the yielding ground, while a minor concern for pure sprinters, can paradoxically reward a horse who settles into their stride rather than fighting for position. Harry's Hill, with 2 course wins at 5f on Good and strong recent form including a win 9 days ago, has the tactical gear to track any loose leader and potentially pounce late from a prominent position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Raid Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely burns bright enough and long enough to drag the prominent types into the battle, leaving a fast-finishing hold-up horse to arrive from the rear.
scenarios.body: Bad Boy Rizz is the legitimate hold-up sprinter here with a proven profile in 5f races on soft-sided ground and a strong record at OR 79, making him the best-credentialled closer if the race truly falls apart; Cuban Grey has been placed in similar conditions but his recent form has been inconsistent. The three redistributed hold-up types — Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, and Asdana — will not be running from their true position and their chances in this scenario are tempered accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate rather than fierce and a midfield runner tracks the leaders before producing a well-timed challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A less-than-expected tempo would compress the field and allow a horse with good tactical awareness to sit in a pocket mid-race and quicken when daylight appears; Buddy Batt's profile — placed at 5f on soft-sided going, ridden by Ronan Whelan — suits this if the fractions ease. Happy Henry has genuine ability when allowed to race from his preferred position and his trainer has had 3 winners from 19 in the 14-day window, but the race shape is likely to push him forward out of his ideal running style.

watchPoints.text: Namiid and Prairie Girl — both prominent types who are directly profiled to benefit if Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now burn each other out; watch whether the leaders are still travelling at the 2f marker or already under maximum pressure.

Harry's Hill — his course-and-going record (14/15, 2W3P) is the best statistical fit in the race and a 9-day turnaround after a win here is worth monitoring closely; if the pace softens even slightly he becomes a serious threat from a prominent position.

Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now — watch the early exchanges from the gates; if one breaks cleanly and clears immediately the dynamic shifts sharply toward a front-running scenario, but any battle for the rail could drain both within two furlongs on yielding ground.

Bad Boy Rizz — the Shane Foley booking stands out for a hold-up sprinter and warrants attention; he will need genuine pace collapse and a clean run to arrive in time, so his finishing position in the final 100 yards is a key read on whether the race truly fell apart at the front.

Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, and Asdana — all three are natural hold-up types who will be racing closer to the pace than ideal; if any of them are seen pulling early or racing in an uncomfortable position mid-race, discount their chance further.

runners_data.name: Ventriloquist

runners_data.name: Zadawa

races.paceDynamic: Zadawa and Mawhibah are confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the off, creating a genuine, honest gallop over this extended 1m4½f trip on yielding ground at Bellewstown. With two genuine pace-setters pushing each other through the early and middle stages, the race will be truly run — neither can afford to ease up and surrender the front — meaning the tempo should be honest enough to stretch the field out and expose those who lack stamina. This shape classically suits hold-up horses and prominent racers who can travel within their comfort zone before unleashing a sustained run from the home turn, rewarding horses with a strong finishing kick over a genuinely-run distance on ease in the ground. This field also contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Fraher Field, Nugentstown Sue, and Cosmetic are redistributed to midfield in the model because they cannot all find their natural position, with Fraher Field (most experienced) and Cosmetic (O'Brien support) likeliest to secure the best of those rear-group slots in practice; prominent-style Shemiyka has the clearest path to a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Zadawa and Mawhibah burn each other off at a genuine clip on yielding ground, setting up a strong-staying finisher.
scenarios.body: The honest duel up front burns stamina reserves early, leaving the race wide open for a horse who has been travelling economically through the race before producing a sustained run from the home turn; yielding ground rewards those with a long, grinding stride rather than a quick turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Survive
scenarios.trigger: If Zadawa or Mawhibah dictates at a deceptively moderate tempo and the lead pair conserve enough energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: One front-runner shakes clear of the other through the final bend and the yielding ground slows the finishing kick of the hold-up horses enough that the lead is never fully pegged back; the winner will be whoever of Zadawa and Mawhibah shows the most tactical intelligence and stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Shemiyka or a lightly-raced unknown tracks the pace prominently and produces the decisive move rounding into the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse in the prominent position avoids the traffic risks that plagued the redistributed hold-up types and times its run off the genuine gallop to claim the spoils before the closers can organise; Shemiyka has course-and-distance form at similar trips in comparable going and Colin Keane's positional riding is a key asset here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Box-Seat Fail
scenarios.trigger: If traffic congestion or a slow first bend traps the redistributed hold-up horses and the field strings out too early for them to recover.
scenarios.body: Nugentstown Sue and Cosmetic, already racing out of their natural role, find themselves further back than ideal with no room to manoeuvre, leaving the race to those who had clean passage throughout; Ventriloquist and Ocean Fire, lightly raced and unknown, could outrun their prices if the race suits a fresh eye.

watchPoints.text: Zadawa and Mawhibah will clash for the lead from the start — watch whether one surrenders early or whether they genuinely press each other through the first half-mile, as the outcome of that duel defines the entire race shape.

Pampar Lady's record on similar ground (3W8P from 15 comparable runs) is unusually strong for this grade — if Gary Carroll gets a clean passage from a hold-up position she is the most proven finisher in the field on this surface.

Kigalienne and Helen's Blaze are both going-unknown debutants or lightly-raced unknowns with top-tier jockey bookings (Foley, McDonogh) — unexposed types at this trip on an ease in ground can spring surprises in maiden company.
Nugentstown Sue's 272-day absence combined with the fades-in-finish flag and redistribution out of her natural role makes her a serious lay candidate — monitor in-running if she is punted.|

Shemiyka's headgear (visor) is worn today for the first time or returned — monitor whether it produces the expected positive response in the early stages, as her prominent style is the cleanest stylistic fit to the pace shape created by the two front-runners.|

races.name: Gibney's Of Malahide (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Baltic Bird
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with solid form at distances of 2m+ on good ground, recording 1W4P from 15 runs in similar conditions; at 7 years old this trip and the yielding surface suit well, and racing from her natural position at the rear is a key advantage in this pace-contested shape.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 15f on good ground gives confidence at this trip; a natural closer whose 1W4P record in similar going conditions is solid, and jockey Mr P J Cawley on a 7lb claim adds value — watch for a late rattle from the back if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: Good recent placed form at 15f on good ground and an impressive 3W7P record in similar conditions; though this horse's instinct is to come from well off the pace, the volume of closers in this field means Friary Road will likely be forced to race more prominently than ideal, which tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Stamina question mark looms large — recent form includes a fade at 16f and the horse is dropping back here to this stiff trip after shorter runs; the ⚠ finish-fade flag is a genuine concern over 2m1½f on yielding ground, and natural hold-up style is compromised by the crowded rear.

runners_data.name: Jerandme
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old veteran whose 0W2P record from 15 starts in similar going reflects honesty without a win; his true instinct is to close from the back but this congested field will push him toward midfield, dulling his most effective weapon, and 103 days off the track adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Sequoiaspirit
runners_data.note: Two wins in soft/good-to-soft conditions from 15 starts in similar going, including a win over 20f on soft, make the yielding ground genuinely appealing; like several rivals, this horse's closing style is squeezed toward midfield by the field's composition, but the going profile is a legitimate positive angle.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners, last won over 23f on good ground which shows the stamina is there; the concern is a rival in Miss Gitana willing to fight for the lead, meaning Catalani cannot dictate entirely on his own terms and the contested fractions could prove costly late.

runners_data.name: Day Trader
runners_data.note: Young 5-year-old whose best recent effort was a 2nd over 12f on soft, but stepping up sharply in trip to 2m1½f on yielding ground is a significant ask; a true hold-up horse who will be operating out of his natural position in this field and the STYLE_FIT flag should temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Only 5 days since last run is eye-catching for a 4-year-old, and previous win over 13f on good ground suggests promise; naturally wants to come from off the pace, but with visor (headgear noted) and a tight turnaround, fitness and stamina over this marathon trip are questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, with 1W5P in similar going and recent placed form over 15-16f; she will press Catalani for the lead throughout, and on yielding ground the likelihood of both leaders flattening out in the straight is real — everything depends on how much she has in reserve.

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Two career wins over 16f on good ground and 2W3P from 13 similar-going starts make this an honest stayer; naturally wants to close from the rear but crowded hold-up division forces a more prominent position, and 18 days since last run for trainer John E & Thomas Kiely who have a single run in the 14-day window.

races.paceDynamic: Catalani and Miss Gitana are the confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 2m1½f trip on yielding ground at Bellewstown, creating an honest, pressured gallop that is unlikely to relent given both have tactical speed and genuine front-running intent. The contested pace will string the field out early, burning off horses who lack the class or stamina to sustain a strong gallop on softening ground, and will reward those with the physical reserves to finish through the final two furlongs. This field carries a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Friary Road, Sequoiaspirit, Jerandme, Day Trader, Cooley's Mist, and Liberated Light are all genuine closers redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field simply cannot accommodate them all, meaning several will be forced to race closer than ideal and their finishing kicks may be compromised. The tactical verdict is clear: with two honest front-runners setting a genuine gallop on yielding ground over a stiff staying trip, the race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up horses with proven stamina and good going form — provided they can secure a clean passage in a bunched midfield pack, those racing closest to their natural style (Baltic Bird, Boxing Great) carry the biggest positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Catalani and Miss Gitana burn each other off at a genuine gallop and the closers find daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a strong honest gallop on yielding ground, leaving them vulnerable entering the final quarter-mile, and the genuine hold-up horses who have sat patiently off the pace finish best of all.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Catalani or Miss Gitana gains a clear advantage early and the other capitulates, allowing a solo front-runner to control tempo.
scenarios.body: With only one horse dictating from the front, the pace becomes more manageable and the leader conserves energy to repel late challengers on this flat, yielding track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the yielding ground slows the contest into a stamina test and the field compresses into a slow-burn trudge through the final mile.
scenarios.body: A dawdle that quickens late suits horses with a proven turn of foot on soft-ish ground and strong form over distances of 2m+, while flat-track speedsters find the mud-slog beyond them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Pacers Fade Late
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners set a suicidal early gallop and completely collapse in the straight, leaving the race to whoever has been forced closest to the action.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed to midfield from their natural hold-up position — Cooley's Mist, Day Trader, Jerandme — find themselves ideally placed through no design of their own and pick up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Watch Catalani and Miss Gitana in the first half-mile — if both are committed to the front and neither yields, the fractions over yielding ground will be genuinely testing and both could be spent before the straight.

The redistribution of six hold-up horses into midfield creates a serious traffic risk from the final turn — Baltic Bird and Boxing Great, as genuine closers ideally placed, could be blocked if the pack compresses and fails to fan out.

Sequoiaspirit's two wins on soft/yielding ground are a notable form angle that may be underweighted in the market — if conditions are riding more testing than the Good to Soft official description suggests, this horse's going profile becomes more relevant.

Jerandme at age 12 and 103 days off the track is the most significant fitness unknown in the field — if showing any ring rust early, the horse will struggle to land a blow even if the pace collapses perfectly.

Cooley's Mist returning on just 5 days' rest is unusual for a 4-year-old stepping up dramatically in trip — if jockey Mr H C Swan is positive and rides with confidence, the quick turnaround may signal stable confidence, but the distance jump from 13f to 2m1½f is the critical question.
